market_context: United States/Canada; household washer resets and basic troubleshooting with a clear distinction between a temporary control glitch and a fault that needs diagnosis.
title: How to Reset a Washing Machine

seo.title: How to Reset a Washing Machine and When Resetting Is Not Enough
seo.meta_description: Learn how to cancel a cycle, power-cycle a washer safely, preserve error codes and recognize when the machine needs troubleshooting instead of another reset.
seo.search_intent: Reset a washer that is frozen or unresponsive without confusing a control reset with a repair of the underlying problem.

excerpt: To reset a washing machine, first try Pause or Cancel if the controls respond. If the panel is still frozen, turn the washer off, disconnect power for about 1–5 minutes, then restore power. Exact steps vary by model. If the same error code returns, stop resetting and troubleshoot the cause instead.
content_html:
A washer that freezes on one screen, ignores Start or seems stuck between stages naturally sends people looking for a reset button. Many machines do not have one. What users call a reset is usually one of three different actions: pausing or canceling a cycle, unlocking the controls, or removing power long enough to restart the electronics.

That distinction matters because a reset may clear a temporary control glitch, but it will not repair a kinked hose, blocked pump, door-lock fault or electrical supply problem.

Before removing power, read what the washer is telling you

If the display shows an error code, write it down or take a photo before you turn the machine off. Samsung specifically notes that a reset can clear stored error information without fixing the condition that caused it. If the code comes back, that repeat is useful diagnostic information.

Also look for a padlock or key icon. Control Lock can make an otherwise normal washer appear unresponsive. The exact way to disable it varies by model, so use the markings on the panel or the owner’s manual.

If you only need to stop the cycle, use Pause or Cancel

If you chose the wrong program, loaded an item by mistake or simply need to stop the wash, you do not need to cut power immediately.

Many machines use Start/Pause, Power/Cancel or a similar control. Whirlpool notes that on some models, holding Start/Pause or Power/Cancel for a few seconds cancels the program and lets the washer drain before it unlocks.

Do not force the door. If water is still in the drum or the basket is moving, the lock is doing a safety job. Let the machine complete its stop or drain sequence.

How to perform a basic power-cycle reset

If the panel is frozen or the washer is behaving oddly after a power interruption, a simple power cycle is reasonable.

  1. Turn the washer off using the Power button if it responds.
  2. Unplug it. If the plug is inaccessible or the washer is hard-wired, switch off the dedicated breaker.
  3. Wait about 1–5 minutes. Samsung and Whirlpool both use this general range in reset guidance.
  4. Restore power and turn the washer back on.
  5. Select a short cycle or the cycle you need and watch for normal behavior.

There is no universal button sequence that works across brands. If your manual lists a specific control reset, factory reset or calibration routine, follow that procedure rather than copying steps from another model.

A power reset is not the same as a factory reset

Removing power restarts the electronic control. A factory reset, available only on certain machines, may erase saved cycles, connectivity settings or other preferences.

Do not perform a factory reset as a routine response to a one-time glitch unless you know what settings it will change.

If the door stays locked, do not pull on it

A washer door may remain locked while water is still in the tub or while the control thinks the cycle has not finished. Try Cancel/Drain if the controls respond. If they do not, use the manufacturer-recommended power cycle.

If water is visible after the reset, the underlying issue may be drainage. At that point, troubleshooting the drain hose, accessible filter or pump path is more useful than repeatedly trying to unlock the door.

What it means if the reset only works once

If the washer returns to normal after you power it off but fails again on the next cycle, it has not actually been repaired. The reset only cleared the temporary control state.

Pay attention to when the problem comes back: during fill, wash, drain or spin. That pattern tells you far more than another reset.

When to check the electrical supply

If the washer will not power on after the reset, confirm that the outlet is live and the breaker has not tripped. Avoid extension cords or adapters that the manufacturer does not approve.

If the breaker trips again, you smell burning, see sparks or the cord is damaged, stop using the machine and have it inspected. Repeatedly resetting a tripped circuit can hide a real electrical fault.

When to stop resetting and start troubleshooting

Move on to diagnosis if the same code keeps returning, the washer will not fill or drain, the door will not lock, the machine stops at the same point every cycle or the panel stays dead even though the outlet has power.

Service is also appropriate when the manual identifies the code as technician-level or when the fault involves wiring, the control board, motor or other internal components that are not routine household maintenance.

The useful rule: reset once, then observe

A good reset is not a sequence of random button combinations. Preserve any code first, rule out Control Lock, cancel the cycle if that is all you need, then remove power for a few minutes if the controls remain unresponsive.

If the problem returns, the next step is not another reset. It is finding the condition that is making the washer fail again.

faq.question: How long should I unplug a washing machine to reset it?
faq.answer: Many manufacturers suggest about 1–5 minutes for a power cycle, but your model’s manual takes priority.

faq.question: Will resetting clear an error code?
faq.answer: It may clear the code from the display or visible memory without fixing the cause. Record the code before cutting power.

faq.question: Do all washers have a Reset button?
faq.answer: No. Many use a power cycle or a model-specific procedure instead of a dedicated Reset button.

faq.question: What if the door is still locked after a reset?
faq.answer: Do not force it. If water remains inside, try Cancel/Drain and troubleshoot a possible drainage problem. Use the model’s emergency-release instructions if provided.
